## Phase 2: `spec/requests` & Request-Specific Shared Infrastructure

### Post-Phase-1 vs. Optimized Metrics (`spec/requests`)

*(Note: Even after Phase 1's shared logging, `Devise::Encryptor` memoization, and `RedisTestTracker` improvements were already active, `spec/requests` still took **139.4s**; pre-Phase-1 baseline with `verbose_query_logs = true` and `:debug` logging was substantially higher at >200s.)*

| Metric | Post-Phase-1 (`spec/requests`) | After Phase 2 (`spec/requests`) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec files / Examples | 263 files / 1,877 examples | 263 files / 1,877 examples | 0 failures |
| Wall-clock runtime (`--seed 12345`) | **139.4s** (2m 19.4s) | **45.0s–48.1s** (avg ~48.1s across seeds) | **~65.5% faster (~2.9x)** vs. Post-Phase-1 (**>75% faster** vs. Pre-Phase-1) |
| Combined `spec/models` + `spec/requests` | >330s Pre-Phase-1 / 171.2s Post-Phase-1 | **~79.9s** (`31.9s` + `48.0s`) | **>4x faster** vs. Baseline (**~2.15x faster** vs. Post-Phase-1) |
| `StackProf` wall samples | 157,943 samples | 52,916 samples | ~66.5% reduction |
| `RSpec` `before` setup samples | 102,659 (65.0% of total) | 19,773 samples | ~80.7% reduction (~5.2x) |
| Factory calls (`FactoryProf`) | 11,030 total (106.7s) | 3,899 total (21.7s) | **~64.7% fewer calls / ~79.7% less factory time** |

#### Slowest Request Spec Groups: Post-Phase-1 vs. After Phase 2

| Spec File | Post-Phase-1 | After Phase 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/requests/cache_spec.rb` (258 ex) | 29.52s | ~3.35s |
| `spec/requests/activitypub/replies_spec.rb` (45 ex) | 13.29s | ~1.60s |
| `spec/requests/signature_verification_spec.rb` (30 ex) | 6.66s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/api/v2/notifications_spec.rb` (29 ex) | 5.57s | ~0.74s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/notifications_spec.rb` (22 ex) | 4.16s | ~0.49s |
| `spec/requests/activitypub/contexts_spec.rb` (7 ex) | 3.10s | ~0.38s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/statuses_spec.rb` (36 ex) | 3.09s | ~1.20s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/timelines/public_spec.rb` (12 ex) | 2.85s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/admin/reports_spec.rb` (25 ex) | 2.32s | ~0.58s |
| `spec/requests/activitypub/outboxes_spec.rb` (14 ex) | 2.16s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/admin/accounts_spec.rb` (46 ex) | 2.14s | ~1.02s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/timelines/link_spec.rb` (11 ex) | 2.11s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/accounts_spec.rb` (20 ex) | 2.04s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/api/v1/timelines/tag_spec.rb` (11 ex) | 2.02s | < 0.30s |
| `spec/requests/statuses_spec.rb` (29 ex) | 1.92s | ~0.92s |

---

### Root Causes Identified & Fixed in Phase 2

`StackProf` wall-time profiling of `spec/requests` revealed that **only 14.4% (~20s out of 139.4s)** was spent inside `ActionDispatch::Integration::Session#process` (actual HTTP requests); over **81% (~113s)** was spent in per-example test setup, inline Sidekiq jobs, route table reloads, crypto PEM parsing, Paperclip post-processing, and `Rack::Attack` middleware overhead:

1. **Inline Sidekiq Execution on Request Setup & Mutations (~29.2% / ~40s of Post-Phase-1)**
   - `type: :request` still defaulted to `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` in `spec/rails_helper.rb`. `TriggerWebhookWorker#perform` alone consumed **24.4%** of `spec/requests` (38,584 / 157,943 samples), plus `DistributionWorker`, `LocalNotificationWorker`, and `ActivityPub::DistributionWorker`.
   - **Fix**: Extended `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` default to `type: :request` in `spec/rails_helper.rb` and `spec/support/test_prof.rb` (including `Sidekiq::Worker.clear_all` and clearing ActiveJob test queue after `before_all` so setup jobs never leak into examples). Audited all positive and negative Sidekiq/mailer/timeline/notification assertions and tagged only the 7 specific example groups that depend on synchronous Sidekiq workers (`api/v1/conversations_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/favourites_spec.rb` unfavourite, `api/v1/timelines/home_spec.rb`, `api/v1/timelines/list_spec.rb`, `api/v1/notifications_spec.rb`, `api/v2/notifications_spec.rb`, and `api/v2/notifications/accounts_spec.rb`) with `sidekiq: :inline`.

2. **Paperclip Style Processing & `Instance` Materialized View Refreshes in Request Specs**
   - Extended `spec/support/paperclip.rb` (`:paperclip_processing`) and `spec/support/domain_materializable.rb` (`:refresh_instances_view`) to `type: %i(model request)`.
   - Tagged `POST /api/v1/media` (`spec/requests/api/v1/media_spec.rb`) and `POST /api/v2/media` (`spec/requests/api/v2/media_spec.rb`) with `:paperclip_processing` where `:small` thumbnails and `video/webm` -> `gifv` transcoding are asserted.

3. **`Rack::Attack` Middleware Overhead on Every Request (`spec/support/rack_attack.rb`, `:rack_attack` tag)**
   - `Rack::Attack` ran on all ~2,200 HTTP requests in `spec/requests`: querying `IpBlock` in PostgreSQL after every `Rails.cache.clear`, authenticating OAuth tokens a second time via `Doorkeeper::OAuth::Token.authenticate` before controllers ran `doorkeeper_authorize!`, and evaluating 18 throttle rules—while only `spec/config/initializers/rack/attack_spec.rb` actually tests `Rack::Attack`.
   - **Fix**: Added `spec/support/rack_attack.rb` to disable `Rack::Attack` by default in `type: :request` unless `:rack_attack` metadata is set or `described_class == Rack::Attack` (`spec/config/initializers/rack/attack_spec.rb` remains enabled and passes).

4. **Shared OAuth API Authentication & Role/Scope Shared Examples (`spec/support/api_authentication.rb`, `spec/support/examples/api.rb`)**
   - `shared_context 'with API authentication'` (now used across ~88 API request specs) fabricated a brand-new `User` + `Account` + `Keypair` + 2 `LoginActivity` + `OAuth::Application` + `AccessToken` on every example, including 239 `forbidden for wrong scope` / `forbidden for wrong role` shared examples (11.14s by itself).
   - **Fix**:
     - Updated `spec/support/api_authentication.rb` to create `user`, `client_app`, and default `oauth_token` once per group via `let_it_be` (with `refind: true` for transactional isolation), automatically falling back to fabricating a lightweight `AccessToken` only when `user`, `client_app`, or `scopes` is overridden. Added `user_attributes:` and `application_attributes:` options and replaced duplicated 4-line manual OAuth setups across 23 API request specs with `include_context 'with API authentication'`.
     - Updated `shared_examples 'forbidden for wrong role'` (`spec/support/examples/api.rb`) to update `user`'s `role_id` inside the example transaction when `user` is inherited from `with API authentication` instead of fabricating 72 separate users + accounts + tokens.

5. **Repeated RSA Key Parsing & Per-Example Route Reloading**
   - Memoized parsed `OpenSSL::PKey` objects in `spec/support/signing_keys_helpers.rb` (eliminating repeated PEM parsing across ActivityPub HTTP-signed requests).
   - In `spec/requests/signature_verification_spec.rb`, moved `Rails.application.routes.draw` and `Rails.application.reload_routes!` from per-example `before`/`after` hooks (which reloaded the entire Mastodon route table 30 times, costing ~5.0s) to `before(:all)`/`after(:all)` while keeping `stub_const` per-example, cutting that spec from 6.66s to <0.30s.

6. **Shared Read-Only Fixture Graphs in Slowest Request Specs (`before_all` & `let_it_be`)**
   - Restructured repeated per-example `before` / `let!` setups into `before_all` / `let_it_be` in the heaviest request specs (`cache_spec.rb` [258 examples: 29.52s -> 3.35s], `activitypub/replies_spec.rb` [13.29s -> 1.60s], `api/v2/notifications_spec.rb` [5.57s -> 0.74s], `api/v1/notifications_spec.rb` [4.16s -> 0.49s], `activitypub/contexts_spec.rb` [3.10s -> 0.38s], `api/v1/timelines/public_spec.rb`, `api/v1/timelines/link_spec.rb`, `api/v1/timelines/tag_spec.rb`, `activitypub/outboxes_spec.rb`, `activitypub/collections_spec.rb`, `accounts_spec.rb`, `statuses_spec.rb`, `statuses/activity_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/quotes_spec.rb`, `api/v1/conversations_spec.rb`, `api/v2/notifications/accounts_spec.rb`, `api/v1/admin/reports_spec.rb`) without modifying any example assertions.
   - **Important note for Redis-backed feeds**: Do **not** move Redis feed population (such as `HomeFeed` in `api/v1/timelines/home_spec.rb` or `ListFeed` in `api/v1/timelines/list_spec.rb`) into `before_all`, because `RedisTestTracker.flush_if_dirty!` flushes Redis between examples.

---

## Shared RSpec Metadata Tags Reference

| Tag | Applies To | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sidekiq: :inline` / `sidekiq: :fake` | All specs | `:fake` for `:model` & `:request`; `:inline` otherwise | Opt into synchronous Sidekiq worker execution only when testing inline worker side-effects |
| `:paperclip_processing` | `:model`, `:request` | Skipped (`false`) | Run real `Paperclip::Attachment#post_process_styles` (`vips`/`ffmpeg`/`blurhash`) |
| `:refresh_instances_view` | `:model`, `:request` | Skipped (`false`) | Run `DomainMaterializable#refresh_instances_view` (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY instances`) |
| `:rack_attack` | `:request` | Disabled (`false`), except `described_class == Rack::Attack` | Enable `Rack::Attack` throttling/blocklist middleware during request specs |

---

## Future Phase Plan: Phase 3 — Factories (`spec/fabricators/`)

*(Do not apply until the dedicated factory optimization phase.)*

Even after Phases 1 and 2, `FactoryProf` shows that `Fabricate` still accounts for **25.5s / 31.9s (~80%)** of `spec/models` (2,869 calls) and **21.7s / 49.8s (~44%)** of `spec/requests` (3,899 calls), largely due to unnecessary cascading associations and `after_create` callbacks in core fabricators:

1. **`spec/fabricators/status_fabricator.rb` (Top priority!)**
   - Lines 10–12 unconditionally run:
     ```ruby

       Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status)
     end
     ```

   - Thus **every single `Fabricate(:status)` secretly creates a `Bookmark`, a second `Account`, a second `User`, a second `Keypair`, and 2 extra `LoginActivity` rows**!
   - Impact measured by `FactoryProf`:
     - `spec/models`: 441 of 445 bookmarks came from this hook (costing **5.4s** post-Phase-1).
     - `spec/requests`: 339 of 348 bookmarks came from this hook (costing **3.8s** post-Phase-2, and accounting for >55% of `Fabricate(:status)`'s 7.0s cost).
   - Removing this `after_create` (and adding explicit `Fabricate(:bookmark)` only in the few specs—likely export/archive/cleanup specs—that actually test bookmarks on statuses) will dramatically speed up the entire test suite.

2. **`spec/fabricators/user_fabricator.rb`**
   - Lines 16–18 unconditionally run:
     ```ruby
     after_create do |user|
       2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity, user: user) }
     end
     ```
   - Creates 2 unused `LoginActivity` rows on every `User` creation (256 rows in `spec/models` and 882 rows in `spec/requests` even after `let_it_be`). Move to a trait/child fabricator or only fabricate `login_activity` in specs testing login activities/retention.

3. **`spec/fabricators/account_fabricator.rb`**
   - Line 14 builds a full `User` (`Fabricate.build(:user, account: nil)`) for every local `Account` (`domain.nil?`), triggering `User#set_approved`, `UserRole.everyone`, `UsernameBlock.matches?`, `EmailDomainBlock.requires_approval?`, `UnreservedUsernameValidator`, and `LoginActivity` callbacks even when specs only test `Account`-level behavior (`User#set_approved` + `UsernameBlock.matches?` alone are still ~4% of `spec/requests` wall samples). ### Key Bottlenecks Fixed

1. **Default `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` for `type: :request` (`spec/rails_helper.rb`, `spec/support/test_prof.rb`)**:
   - Inline Sidekiq jobs accounted for ~29.2% of post-Phase-1 `spec/requests` wall time (`TriggerWebhookWorker#perform` alone was 24.4%).

6. **Documentation (`docs/RSPEC_OPTIMIZATION.md`)**:
